newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia completes conversion to scripless trading.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia completes conversion to scripless trading.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) said on Tuesday that it had essentially completed the conversion of all listed company shares into scripless trading and settlement by the end of 1996.

In a statement, the KLSE said the one exception was property concern Amanah Harta Tanah PNB, which requested a postponement to amend its trust deed to comply with the requirements of the Central Depository System, the scripless system.

Under the conversion, the KLSE said it has eliminated the laborious and "risk-fraught" task of physically clearing trades, and said investors could now use automatic registration of shares upon purchase.
The KLSE also said the move would cut costs.
"It represents a milestone for the Malaysian securities industry," the statement said. The move to convert from a certificate-based system to one based on computer records started in March 1993.
The scripless system is operated by the KLSE's subsidiary company, Malaysian Central Depository Sdn Bhd.
The move to a paperless system will also allow the Malaysian bourse to consider other developments, including shortening the settlement period for trading.
